content:
To clarify some details about the tank explosion below the Bridge of the Americas which passes over the Panama Canal yesterday:

- The explosions were primarily due to two fuel tanker trucks blowing up
- There is no evidence of catastrophic secondary explosions from the tank farm itself
- The tank facility dates back to 1916, while the bridge was built in 1962
- A private third party which leases the tank facility had its concession terminated by the Maritime Authority yesterday
- At least one person died, 3 were seriously injured (second degree burns)
- The fire was brought under control in a few hours by Panamanian fire fighters
- The cause of the explosion is believed to be negligence, not terrorism

Some people have commented that the explosion did "not occur at the Panama Canal." This is false. The explosion occurred a few steps from the waterway, directly under the Bridge of the Americas, which passes over the Canal. That being said, no Canal infrastructure appears to have been impacted. 

We are awaiting the structural damage assessment of the Bridge of the Americas itself, as the tanker explosions did cause visible impacts to the bridge itself. 

Right now, the main impacts to Panama are traffic related. Hundreds of thousands of people commute over the Panama Canal from Panama West to the city. The incident has caused massive disruptions due to fewer available lanes, forcing traffic over the Centenario Bridge, and limiting bus availibility. 

The situation could have been much worse, so those of us in Panama are relieved, and awaiting the reopening of the bridge following the declaration that transit is safe.
